title: One Nation vows to ramp up gas exploration in Victoria energy policy
text:
By NICHOLAS COMINO, POLITICAL REPORTER, AUSTRALIA

Published:  15:35 AEST, 31 August 2026   |  Updated:  15:37 AEST, 31 August 2026

31

View  comments

One Nation has vowed to ramp up gas exploration, scrap major renewable projects and roll back a historic ban on nuclear energy as it unveils its new energy policy in Victoria.

Federal leader Pauline Hanson and Victorian leader Warren Pickering launched the policy at the Loy Yang site in the Latrobe Valley on Monday, arguing Victoria needs a more reliable energy mix and a renewed focus on coal and gas.

Under the policy, One Nation would seek to extend some Loy Yang operations beyond its scheduled 2035 closure. The party provided no costings for the plan. The facility supplies 30 per cent of Victoria’s electricity.

Hanson said private investment could play a role in keeping the station open.

Pickering also announced the party would axe both the Western Renewable Energy Zone and the Coastal Renewable Energy Zone if elected, labelling both as ‘ideologically driven nonsense’.

‘The Western Renewable Energy Zone will be abolished, the Coastal Renewable Energy Zone will be abolished,' he said.

'We know it’s ideologically driven nonsense that is dead in the water.'

He added One Nation would instead focus on expanding domestic gas production.

Pauline Hanson (pictured) vowed to keep open the Loy Yang power station ahead of 2035

Pickering also announced the party would axe both the Western Renewable Energy Zone and the Coastal Renewable Energy Zone if elected, labelling both as ‘ideologically driven nonsense’

‘We intend to focus heavily on gas, specifically. We are five years behind on exploration drilling in both the Gippsland and Otway basins for gas reserves,’ he said.

One Nation also pledged to remove VicGrid’s compulsory acquisition powers, arguing the authority should not be able to force landholders to surrender property for transmission projects linked to Victoria’s renewable rollout.

The party’s policy package includes support for offshore gas exploration, new investment in coal-fired power and a push to repeal Victoria’s 1983 ban on nuclear energy.

Loy Yang was among the sites nominated by former Opposition leader Peter Dutton in the Coalition’s federal nuclear energy pitch before this year’s election.

The announcement followed Hanson’s appearance at a ‘Farmers Fight Back’ rally in Marnoo, where she promised to scrap the controversial VNI West transmission network.

The proposed line has become a friction point in regional Victoria, with some landowners objecting to transmission infrastructure being routed across their land.

Hanson also vowed to overturn fines imposed on farmers who refused government planners access to their properties.

‘We’re going to wipe those fines,’ Hanson said.

Loy Yang was among the sites nominated by former Opposition leader Peter Dutton in the Coalition’s federal nuclear energy pitch before this year’s election

‘I’m telling them all, don’t pay the fines, because I think there’s going to be a big change in Victoria come November.’

Hanson said landholders deserved stronger protections.

‘I believe that these people should be given a fair go. They have a right to protect their properties,’ Hanson said.

One Nation said more detailed policies would be released in the coming weeks as the party targets support in regional Victoria ahead of the November state election and capitalises on its recent by-election victory in WA’s Secret Harbour.
